clue.text: He leaves the old city and pinches farm produce

indicators.note: leaves means the word He departs from the clue word beside it, leaving only its remainder

parts.note: taken as written
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, the crossword's favourite old city
to pinch is to nip

explanation.surface: A man quits an ancient city and makes off with crops from the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He leaves the' takes HE out of THE, leaving T; then come UR and NIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Root vegetables grown on farms are a staple field crop.

clue.text: Lone dog loosened inside saddle-strap

indicators.note: inside places the loosened dog within the word for lone

parts.note: lone means single

indicators.note: loosened suggests the letters of the dog word are shaken free and rearranged

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A solitary hound slips free within a horse's harness.
explanation.walkthrough: A surcingle is a girth belt; 'loosened' rearranges the dog word, and 'inside' sets the result after the first letter of the lone word.
explanation.definitionFit: A girth strap passing round a horse's body holds the saddle or a pack in place.

clue.text: The queen's rising fury about upright character

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the assembled letters read from bottom to top
about means the word for fury goes round the letter

parts.note: fury is anger
the letter I is a single upright stroke

explanation.surface: Her Majesty's temper flares around a dignified person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside ANGER to make ANIGER, and 'rising' turns that round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for a reigning female monarch, seen after her name on official documents.

clue.text: Fully explained it was once legal parking inside

indicators.note: inside means the parking letter sits within the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former, what something once was
licit means lawful
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Something formerly allowed now has a car park built into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts the parking letter between the two pieces; 'it' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated clearly and in detail, leaving nothing implied.

clue.text: Re-elect dean into new assembly, with international agreement

indicators.note: a new assembly of the words means their letters are put together again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A dean is voted back into a newly formed body, with a treaty between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new assembly' rearranges the fifteen letters of RE-ELECT DEAN INTO; the 'assembly' looks like a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names the 1904 understanding between Britain and France, and any friendly pact between countries.

clue.text: Report from here on squash, and what they do in the ring

parts.note: to squash is to press

parts.words: what they do in the ring
parts.note: boxers box in a boxing ring

explanation.surface: Journalists file from a squash court, then watch the boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Reporters sit in this enclosure at a sports ground to write their stories.

clue.text: Symbolic white robes worn for one hour in the morning?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: Ceremonial white garments are put on for a single early hour.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the garb of Muslim pilgrims to Mecca; 'worn for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilgrims on the hajj wear two plain white seamless cloths showing purity and equality.

clue.text: This second social worker taken on this month

indicators.note: taken on means the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: inst. is the old business abbreviation for this month
the ant is the crossword's social worker, living in a colony

explanation.surface: A social worker is hired right now this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a case worker but an insect living in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Right now, this very moment, the present split second.

clue.text: Highest ranking copper by order of the court

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a rule is an order made by a court

explanation.surface: A top policeman acts under court orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the senior magistrates had the right to sit on a special ivory chair.

clue.text: Speculate? There is nothing wrong in it

indicators.note: in it means the nothing letter goes inside the jumbled words
wrong signals the letters of there is are set out incorrectly

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone guesses, and insists there is no harm in that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' jumbles THERE IS, and 'in it' sets the nothing letter in the middle of the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To form ideas and conjecture without proof.

clue.text: Carve a design for trendy bed in the home counties

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: in places the bed inside the letters for the region

parts.note: the home counties surround London in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
a crib is a child's bed

explanation.surface: Someone engraves a pattern for a fashionable bed in the counties round London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties around London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave or cut lettering or a pattern into a surface.

clue.text: Boat made by boy with a kitchen utensil

parts.note: Sam is a boy's name
a pan is a cooking pot

explanation.surface: A lad builds a vessel using a cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flat-bottomed craft of Chinese and East Asian waters.

clue.text: Mine may be a duck and a swan, with wild cats

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, written O
a pen is a female swan

indicators.note: wild means the letters of cats run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A duck, a swan and some feral cats claim a patch.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a zero score in cricket; 'wild' turns CATS into CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface pit where ore or coal is dug from the open ground, not tunnelled.

clue.text: A long tee shot — can make it even longer!

indicators.note: shot means the letters are blasted into a new order

explanation.surface: A golfer's long drive off the tee can stretch further still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges A LONG TEE; the golf shot is the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch or lengthen something.

clue.text: Drunken aunt eager to take the pledge

indicators.note: drunken means the letters reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy relative is keen to sign up for temperance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the pledge' means swearing off drink, an apt thing for a drunken aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal promise or assurance that something will be done.

clue.text: It's like glass — six tore around us!

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six

indicators.note: around means the letters of tore are moved round into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Six people rush around us in a fragile scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like it places VI round something, but it only jumbles the letters of 'tore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembling glass in hardness, shine or transparency.

clue.text: I'm to peg out — I caught this disease

indicators.note: out means the letters of the phrase come out in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A patient fears death after catching an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I'M TO PEG together with the second I.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagious bacterial skin infection with crusty sores.

clue.text: Large bird seen to peck Old Testament character

parts.note: the moa was a huge flightless bird of New Zealand
to peck is to bite

explanation.surface: A big bird pecks at a figure from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Moab, like Ruth in the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Head of state happening to go to hospital —— not for the first time

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: an event is a happening
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: A national leader goes into hospital yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of state' looks like a president but supplies only S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinal far along the count, so whatever happens then has happened six times before.

clue.text: Grass infiltrating harbour provided the information

indicators.note: infiltrating means the harbour word gets inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: An informer slips into the docks and passes on what he knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like an informer, which suits the surface, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Gave an account of something, told officially.

clue.text: This boat may be tied up

definitions.text: This boat may be tied up

parts.words: This boat may be tied up
parts.note: a mail-carrying ship shares its name with a small parcel wrapped and tied with string

explanation.surface: A vessel moored at the quay.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail steamer on a regular route shares its name with a small parcel bound with string.

clue.text: Dental trouble? Use salt repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly means the sailor word is written twice over

parts.note: a salt and a tar are both old words for a sailor

explanation.surface: Advice to rinse with salt water for a sore tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like the seasoning but is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard deposit of calcified plaque that builds up on teeth.

clue.text: Though now worthless in Thailand, it raised about a pound

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
ca. abbreviates circa, about
L abbreviates the pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An obsolete Thai coin once fetched about a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns IT into TI in this down entry; 'raised' looks like a sum collected.
explanation.definitionFit: The former silver coin and unit of money of Siam, replaced by the baht.

clue.text: Aroused by something burning on deckhead

parts.note: incense is burnt for its scent
read as the head of deck, its first letter D

explanation.surface: Someone stirred by a burning smell on a ship's ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: A deckhead is the underside of a ship's deck, but here it is split into 'deck head', the first letter of deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Made very angry, inflamed.

clue.text: An easy task, they say — forward a tree!

parts.note: people call an easy task a cinch in slang
on means forward, as in move on

explanation.surface: A simple job, people claim: just push ahead to a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American evergreen whose bark yields quinine.

clue.text: Makes strenuous efforts to get ten trees demolished

indicators.note: demolished means the letters are knocked down and rebuilt in another order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Someone works hard to fell ten trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' rearranges X (ten) and TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: Applies force or energy with effort.

clue.text: Lacking status, banker has to entertain a group of students

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in a guest, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a banker is a river, having banks; the Dee is a British river
a class is a group of students

explanation.surface: A financier hosts a party of pupils despite his lowly standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is not a financier but a river, something with banks: the Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: Having fallen in social standing, from the French for out of one's class.
